text:
🔆🔅 November 6, 2026 – Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, who accompanied SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei during his visit to Moscow, has stressed that any renewed diplomatic engagement with the United States must be based on concrete actions rather than written commitments. He also highlighted the strategic importance of Iran-Russia energy and transit cooperation."

""
"============"

"SOT1, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) – (00:00 - 00:36): "The Islamic Republic of Iran has the right that if wants to enter a new diplomatic arena, it will no longer settle for so-called American 'paper commitments.' We must see concrete action from the United States. These actions involve very clear and tangible measures that the other side must take. Once these measures are put into effect and implemented, the conditions will naturally be in place for opening a new chapter.""

"SOT2, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) – (00:37 - 00:59): "Over the past year and a half, during four rounds of diplomatic negotiations with the United States, the Americans disrupted each round through hostile actions and violations of their commitments, effectively creating an entirely different set of circumstances.""

"SOT3, Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (Farsi) – (01:00 - 01:56): "[On Iran-Russia cooperation in the gas sector and the transit corridor] These two projects are, in practice, strategic initiatives that dispel what could be described as the naive illusion held by certain powers, including the United States, that they can exert pressure on the Islamic Republic of Iran. This is because implementing these projects will make other countries significantly dependent on Iran. Just as the Islamic Republic of Iran, in the period following the third imposed war, made effective use of its geopolitical leverage in the Strait of Hormuz to advance its national interests and contribute to regional security, these two projects represent geoeconomic assets that Iran can strategically leverage to promote development and progress both within the country and across the region, while also strengthening security.
